Subject: RE: Production: sustained 5xxs & token throttling on /v1/generate - immediate help needed

Summary of what I see so far (initial triage):
- Observed pattern: tenant token consumption spiked due to a bot-driven batch job (non-standard burst pattern).
- Rate-control snapshot (captured at 09:58): the tenant's burst window was set to 60 tokens / 10s with an effective per-minute quota that was accidentally left at a legacy, lower value (quota drift).
- The routing policy has a tighter safety gate for the primary model (gptx-128) which triggers fallback/queueing and then 5xxs when the GPU pools saturate.

Root cause hypothesis: a recent rollout to the tenant-specific policy (automated config rollouts) failed to merge default burst allowances, resulting in a split state where burst tokens were low but the router still sent the normal traffic profile. In short: quota/burst misconfiguration + routing safety valve = queue overflow => 500s.

Immediate mitigation I applied at 10:00:
- Elevated burst tokens for greenline-tenant-42 to 300 tokens / 10s (temporary, will revert after stability).
- Added a temporary route that steers 35% of greenline traffic to gptx-lite-64 (lower memory per request, higher QPS).
- Increased enqueue_limit on the primary model pool from 250 -> 600 for the next 2 hours.

Effect: 10:06-10:20 saw a drop in 5xxs and 429s to baseline. Still monitoring.

Next asks:
- Ops: confirm any longer-term quota rollback or update to the tenant policy in config repo.
- Leadership: approve a one-time capacity credit (billing/contract implications) so we can keep the temporary routing if needed.

Logs / artifacts: throttle-config-snapshot.json attached (sample). Jira: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INF-2123

—Marcus

Neha — quick executive summary and approval request.

- Visible impact window: ~08:46 - 10:00 PDT (partial mitigation applied)
- Business impact: production-facing errors for paying customers; some UI retries surfaced errors.

Technical cause (short): configuration drift during a tenant policy rollout left burst allowance at legacy minima while routing remained at normal levels, causing queueing and saturation. Marcus applied emergency measures and saw error rates come down.

Request: approve a one-time quota/credit override and allow temporary routing to remain for up to 24 hours while we complete the RCA and a safe rollback. Billing/contract recommendation: credit one day of peak overage or equivalent credit — Monica can propose the exact terms.

I recommend we also proactively run a config-merge audit on tenant rollouts to prevent recurrence.

Please reply with approval or questions. Wording for customer comms below (we'll wait for your sign-off):
